summary: This study investigates the mechanisms behind the long-term sequelae of retinopathy of prematurity (ROP), a leading cause of childhood blindness, in both human subjects and a rat model. The research focuses on the relationships between neural retina, vasculature, and refractive development abnormalities, with a particular emphasis on the role of rod photoreceptors in initiating poor outcomes. To examine these mechanisms, the study will employ a longitudinal approach in the oxygen-induced retinopathy 'ROP rat' model, using innovative procedures to study the function and structure of the neural retina and its vascular supply, as well as associations with altered refractive development.
